parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: Which Vrbo marketplace to read from. `us` (the default) prices in US dollars, `fr` and `de` in euros, `nz` in New Zealand dollars and `au` in Australian dollars. Each marketplace sets its own prices rather than converting another's, so the same rental can genuinely cost less on one than on another  -  comparing them is a real use for this parameter  -  and the selection of rentals differs slightly between them as well. Wording that Vrbo itself supplies (rating labels, section headings, policy text) comes back in the marketplace's language: French on `fr`, German on `de`. Text written by the host  -  the listing title and description  -  is only translated where that host has supplied a translation, so on many rentals it stays in the language the host wrote it in. Example: `de`.

parameters.name: pinned_property_id
parameters.description: Numeric id of one rental to pull to the very top of the results, e.g. `33493697`. When that rental matches the destination and filters you searched it is returned first on page 1, and every other listing follows in its normal order; nothing else about the page changes. Use it to put a rental you already track side by side with the rest of its market in a single response  -  same dates, same guests, same filters  -  so its price, rating and photo can be read against its direct competitors without a second call. A rental that does not match the search (wrong destination, filtered out, or unavailable for the dates) simply is not pinned, and no error is raised. Omitted by default, in which case results come back in their natural order.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: Which Vrbo marketplace to read from. `us` (the default) prices in US dollars, `fr` and `de` in euros, `nz` in New Zealand dollars and `au` in Australian dollars. Each marketplace sets its own prices rather than converting another's, so the same rental can genuinely cost less on one than on another  -  comparing them is a real use for this parameter  -  and the selection of rentals differs slightly between them as well. Wording that Vrbo itself supplies (rating labels, section headings, policy text) comes back in the marketplace's language: French on `fr`, German on `de`. Text written by the host  -  the listing title and description  -  is only translated where that host has supplied a translation, so on many rentals it stays in the language the host wrote it in. Example: `de`.

query.description: Free-text destination (place name). Used when no `region_id` is given. Provide this or `region_id`.
query.example: Miami Beach, Florida, United States of America

region_id.description: Numeric region id from /locations-autocomplete (`region_id`). Preferred over `query`.

pinned_property_id.description: Numeric id of one rental to pull to the very top of the results, e.g. `33493697`. When that rental matches the destination and filters you searched it is returned first on page 1, and every other listing follows in its normal order; nothing else about the page changes. Use it to put a rental you already track side by side with the rest of its market in a single response  -  same dates, same guests, same filters  -  so its price, rating and photo can be read against its direct competitors without a second call. A rental that does not match the search (wrong destination, filtered out, or unavailable for the dates) simply is not pinned, and no error is raised. Omitted by default, in which case results come back in their natural order.

checkin.description: First night of the stay, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, e.g. `2026-11-05`. Supply it together with `checkout` to get results priced for those nights; omit both to browse a destination without dates.

checkout.description: Departure date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, e.g. `2026-11-08`. Only takes effect when `checkin` is supplied too.

adults.description: Number of adults the rental must sleep. Defaults to `2` when omitted. Example: `4`.

children.description: Ages of the children travelling, each 0 - 17, comma-separated, e.g. `4,7`. Defaults to no children.

price_min.description: Lowest price to keep, in the currency the results are priced in. Compared against the per-night rate by default; set `price_type=total` to compare against the whole-stay total instead. Example: `100`.

price_max.description: Highest price to keep, in the currency the results are priced in. Compared against the per-night rate by default; set `price_type=total` to compare against the whole-stay total instead. Example: `450`.

price_type.description: Chooses what `price_min` / `price_max` are compared against. `nightly` (the default) compares them against the per-night rate; `total` compares them against the all-in total for the selected dates. Example: `total`.

bedrooms.description: Keep only rentals with at least this many bedrooms (0 - 50). No bedroom requirement is applied when omitted. Example: `3`.

bathrooms.description: Keep only rentals with at least this many bathrooms (1 - 50). No bathroom requirement is applied when omitted. Example: `2`.

beds.description: Keep only rentals with at least this many beds (1 - 20), counting every bed of every size. No bed requirement is applied when omitted. Example: `4`.

king_beds.description: Keep only rentals with at least this many king beds (0 - 20). This is a minimum for that one bed size, not an exact count, and it is applied on top of any `beds` total you set rather than instead of it. Combine the bed-type parameters to match a group's sleeping arrangements  -  `king_beds=1&twin_beds=2` keeps rentals that sleep a couple in a king and two children in twins. No king-bed requirement is applied when omitted. Example: `1`.

queen_beds.description: Keep only rentals with at least this many queen beds (0 - 20). A minimum for that one bed size, applied in addition to any `beds` total and to the other bed-type parameters  -  `queen_beds=2` keeps rentals offering two or more queens, whatever else they sleep. Useful for matching a group that needs a set number of double-occupancy rooms. No queen-bed requirement is applied when omitted. Example: `2`.

full_beds.description: Keep only rentals with at least this many full (double) beds (0 - 20). A minimum for that one bed size, applied in addition to any `beds` total and to the other bed-type parameters. Full beds sleep two at a squeeze rather than in comfort, so pair this with `queen_beds` or `king_beds` when a group needs proper double rooms. No full-bed requirement is applied when omitted. Example: `1`.

twin_beds.description: Keep only rentals with at least this many twin (single) beds (0 - 20). A minimum for that one bed size, applied in addition to any `beds` total and to the other bed-type parameters. This is the one to set when a group travels with children or with adults who each need their own bed  -  `twin_beds=4` keeps only rentals that can put four people in separate single beds. No twin-bed requirement is applied when omitted. Example: `2`.

bunk_beds.description: Keep only rentals with at least this many bunk beds (0 - 20). A minimum for that one bed type, applied in addition to any `beds` total and to the other bed-type parameters. A bunk counts as one bed here even though it sleeps two, so it is a strong signal for family and group rentals; `bunk_beds=1` is the usual way to find a rental with a kids' room. No bunk-bed requirement is applied when omitted. Example: `1`.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: Which Vrbo marketplace to read from. `us` (the default) prices in US dollars, `fr` and `de` in euros, `nz` in New Zealand dollars and `au` in Australian dollars. Each marketplace sets its own prices rather than converting another's, so the same rental can genuinely cost less on one than on another  -  comparing them is a real use for this parameter  -  and the selection of rentals differs slightly between them as well. Wording that Vrbo itself supplies (rating labels, section headings, policy text) comes back in the marketplace's language: French on `fr`, German on `de`. Text written by the host  -  the listing title and description  -  is only translated where that host has supplied a translation, so on many rentals it stays in the language the host wrote it in. Example: `de`.

polygon.description: Convenience alternative to the four corner parameters: a list of `lat,lng` points separated by semicolons, at least 3 of them, e.g. `25.76,-80.14;25.79,-80.14;25.79,-80.12;25.76,-80.12`. Because the search itself works in rectangles, a page can come back with fewer than 50 results while `has_more` is still `true`  -  keep paging while `has_more` is `true` rather than stopping when a page looks short.
